BSc Computer Science · Level 5 · Required

Artificial Intelligence Principles (AI4101)

Seven modules that take you from the foundations of intelligent agents to search, optimization, adversarial reasoning, constraint satisfaction, and logical agents.

Modules

  1. 01

    Introduction to Artificial Intelligence

    Concepts, Domains, and Applications · 4 contact hours

    What people mean by "intelligent", what this field actually builds, and the responsibility that comes with it.
  2. 02

    Intelligent Agents and Their Environments

    Agent Designs and Task Environments · 8 contact hours

    The one idea the whole course is built on: something that perceives, decides, and acts.
  3. 03

    Problem Solving by Search

    Uninformed and Informed Search Algorithms · 16 contact hours

    The heart of the course. How an agent that does not know the answer can still find it — first blindly, then with a sense of direction.
  4. 04

    Optimization

    Finding Better Solutions · 8 contact hours

    Turn a real problem into one a computer can score, then search for better and better answers.
  5. 05

    Adversarial Search

    Minimax, Alpha-Beta Pruning, Expectiminimax · 8 contact hours

    Search when somebody else chooses every second move — and they want you to lose.
  6. 06

    Constraint Satisfaction Problems

    Backtracking, Heuristics, Constraint Propagation · 8 contact hours

    Search that looks inside the problem instead of treating each state as a black box — and solves it far faster because of it.
  7. 07

    Logical Agents

    Propositional Logic, First-Order Logic, Resolution · 8 contact hours

    Agents that hold what they know as sentences, and work out what must follow from it.
